clue.text: Emergency transport, used by Procrustes ?

definitions.meaning: a frame for carrying the injured or sick, as ambulance crews do
the Greek bandit Procrustes racked short victims to fit his bed, so his device was a rack that lengthened bodies

explanation.walkthrough: Procrustes of Greek myth made guests fit his bed by lopping the tall and lengthening the short on a rack.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a litter for casualties, and a device for elongating things, which is what the mythical bandit did.

clue.text: Speed-writer ?

parts.note: fast plus an author: Jonathan who wrote Gulliver's Travels has a surname meaning fast

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word it suggests a stenographer, but it combines 'speed' (fast) with the author of Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means quick, and Jonathan of that name was the satirist behind Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Rabbit's kidnap victim has rest disturbed by a cock

parts.note: in Winnie-the-Pooh, Rabbit plots to kidnap Roo, Kanga's baby

indicators.note: the word rest is disturbed, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A kidnapped creature's sleep is broken by a crowing bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh, Rabbit kidnaps baby Roo. 'disturbed' rearranges REST into STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A male farmyard bird that crows at dawn.

clue.text: Primitive community types, the children of Israel?

definitions.meaning: the Israelites were divided into twelve tribes, descended from Jacob's sons

explanation.definitionFit: Members of a clan or people, as the twelve Israelite groups were.

clue.text: For wire-walking. over Niagara the suspense is something electric!

definitions.text: For wire-walking. over Niagara the suspense is something electric!

parts.words: For wire-walking. over Niagara the suspense is something electric!
parts.note: a tightrope walker above the falls creates great suspense up high, and a taut wire is literally under strain; the phrase also describes powerful voltage

explanation.walkthrough: Blondin crossed Niagara Falls on a tightrope: up high the suspense and the strain on the rope are great, and the phrase also means powerful voltage.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical power carried at great voltage, as in pylon cables.

clue.text: Beastly gate-crasher!

parts.note: a male sheep butts through gates, and so does the battering device named after it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' suggests rude behaviour; here it means an animal, the male sheep that butts its way through.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sheep that charges with its horns, also a battering engine.

clue.text: Correspond with a fire-raiser

definitions.meaning: to agree or be equal, as colours do when paired
a small stick tipped with chemical that is struck to light a fire

explanation.definitionFit: To correspond is to be equal or agree; a lucifer stick is what starts a fire.

clue.text: Edouard, an artist chap, and un-British

parts.note: a chap is a man
ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film, is an alien, i.e. foreign

explanation.surface: Edouard is a foreign painter, someone not British.
explanation.walkthrough: ET is the film's extra-terrestrial, so an alien; 'un-British' takes alien in its sense of foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: Edouard of that surname was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: A kiss on Wendy's fingertip

parts.note: in Peter Pan, Peter does not know what a kiss is, so Wendy gives him a sewing cap for a finger and calls it one

explanation.walkthrough: In J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan, Wendy offers Peter a 'kiss' and he holds out his hand, so she gives him the sewing finger-cap instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal cap worn on the finger when sewing, which Wendy calls a kiss.

clue.text: A poor 2 to be so foully treated?

definitions.text: A poor 2 to be so foully treated?

parts.words: A poor 2 to be so foully treated?
parts.note: 2 points to the cock of 2-down; a male bird bullied by hens, with 'foully' punning on fowl

explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to 2-down, a cock. A cock nagged by its hens has been nagged by fowls, and 'foully' sounds like 'fowl-ly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man dominated by a nagging wife is like a cock attacked by hens' beaks.

clue.text: I call round on pressing business

indicators.note: the word for call goes around the little word on

parts.note: to call someone is to telephone, or ring, them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drops by on an urgent matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' looks like 'urgent' but means smoothing clothes with a hot iron; 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot flat-iron is household laundry work.

clue.text: One of Hudson's greenhouses

parts.note: Split 'greenhouses' as green houses and one such house is a grand dwelling

explanation.walkthrough: W. H. Hudson's 1904 novel is Green Mansions, so a single 'green house' of his is a stately home, not a glasshouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately residence is a house, and Hudson's title calls such houses green.

clue.text: It is to be returned before the tenth

indicators.note: returned here means sent back, so the word It is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something borrowed must be given back before the tenth of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be returned' turns IT round; 'before' only sets it ahead of THE. A tithe was a tenth of produce paid to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A church levy was historically a tenth of one's produce or income.

clue.text: Bradshaw came across Jack in a top-hat

indicators.note: the top-hat lies across, i.e. spans, the other letters inside it

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat, especially a silk top hat
with 'across' used as the container signal, came gives the letters of met
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: A man named Bradshaw bumped into a friend called Jack wearing a top hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bradshaw's Railway Guide was the standard British railway schedule for a century. MET and AB go inside TILE, old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradshaw was the famous Victorian railway guide listing train departures.

clue.text: Will it even mean the end of Scotland Yard?

definitions.text: Will it even mean the end of Scotland Yard?

parts.words: Will it even mean the end of Scotland Yard?
parts.note: the London police headquarters is named after a unit of length that conversion to metres would abolish

explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police; switching to metric units would abolish the yard as a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting to the metre and kilogram system, which replaces yards, feet and pounds.

clue.text: Lady's man?

parts.note: not a womaniser: the male counterpart of the title Lady, as a knight's wife is styled Lady

explanation.walkthrough: A 'ladies' man' is a charmer, but here the man matching a Lady is the titled knight or baronet she is married to.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a knight is called Lady, and he carries the matching honorific.

clue.text: Small plantation's latex product in short

indicators.note: the latex product goes inside the word for short

parts.note: shy can mean short of, lacking, as in two shy of a dozen
rubber is made from latex, the sap of the rubber tree

explanation.surface: A small estate's rubber output is in short supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plantation' suggests a rubber estate but means a planting of bushes; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A planted area of bushes in a garden.

clue.text: For grill-room customer with tiny appetite ?

definitions.text: For grill-room customer with tiny appetite ?

parts.words: For grill-room customer with tiny appetite ?
parts.note: minute can mean very small, so a quick-cooked thin cut of beef is jokingly for a small eater

explanation.walkthrough: A thin cut of beef cooked in about sixty seconds is named for its cooking time, but 'minute' (my-NEWT) also means tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin slice of beef fried very briefly on a grill.

clue.text: Complaint turns awkward in Peterborough district

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the name of the district

parts.note: the Soke of Peterborough was a historic administrative district of England

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of turns fall in a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: A grumble that the bends are tricky in an English region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Soke of Peterborough was an old English administrative area. 'awkward' is the anagram signal, 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat illness from too much sun is an ailment, and complaint means an ailment.

clue.text: Put fresh life into a company in a dramatic interpretation

indicators.note: company goes inside the word for the dramatic interpretation

parts.note: a rendition is a performance or interpretation of a play or piece

explanation.surface: A director revives a theatre troupe through a bold new staging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put fresh life into' looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a machine or building is to restore it to working order, giving it new life.

clue.text: Fancy him entering a crooked race!

indicators.note: the word him goes into the scrambled letters
a crooked race is dishonest, but here race is bent into a new letter order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Imagine him taking part in a rigged contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' is the anagram signal, giving CERA, and 'entering' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful illusion or wild dream, a figment of imagination.

clue.text: Fox Mr Sloan

definitions.meaning: an old dialect word for a fox, as in Reynard
... Sloan was a famous American jockey of the 1890s

explanation.walkthrough: Tod Sloan, an American jockey who rode in England around 1900, gave rise to the rhyming slang 'on your tod' (alone).
explanation.definitionFit: A northern English dialect name for the fox, and the first name of the celebrated jockey.

clue.text: Mediterranean port, £2 variety

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means a different arrangement of them

parts.note: the pound sign is L (from libra) and 2 in Roman numerals is II

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean harbour offering a two-pound assortment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges PORT with L and II. 'port' is both fodder and part of the sense: the city is a Mediterranean port, so 'Mediterranean' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Libyan capital lies on the Mediterranean coast, as does the Lebanese city of that name.

clue.text: Appropriate sort of metal for a 50p piece?

definitions.text: Appropriate sort of metal for a 50p piece?

parts.words: Appropriate sort of metal for a 50p piece?
parts.note: a tin-based pewter alloy shares its name with the seated female figure shown on the British fifty-pence coin

explanation.walkthrough: The UK 50p coin long carried the seated figure personifying Britain, and a pewter-like alloy shares her name, so that metal would be 'appropriate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A silvery tin alloy named after the female personification of Britain, who featured on the 50p coin.

clue.text: It's wrong for an unmarried girl

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
a miss is an unmarried girl or woman

explanation.surface: Is it wrong to address a young woman as a miss?
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of order or faulty has gone awry.

clue.text: They chase the bull

parts.note: in the zodiac, Gemini follows Taurus the bull

explanation.walkthrough: Not a bullfight: Gemini comes straight after Taurus in the zodiac, so the pair 'chase' the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the zodiac pair, is the sign that follows Taurus.

clue.text: There's some point in body covering-some wool?

indicators.note: the point goes inside the body covering

parts.note: skin covers the body
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A sheepskin has a sharp bit hidden in its wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E, a compass point, inside SKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiled length of yarn is how wool is sold.

clue.text: A lonely man before taking the widow's offer

parts.note: ere is an old word meaning before
in the Gospel story the poor widow gave her mite, a tiny coin

explanation.surface: A solitary fellow, about to accept a widow's proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: The widow's mite is the small offering praised by Jesus in Mark and Luke.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious recluse or hermit lives alone in solitude.

clue.text: Journalist without money in old age

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the journalist goes round the money

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist
L stands for libra, the pound sterling

explanation.surface: A hack reaches his old age penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside', so ED goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for age or old times.

clue.text: Elementary form is nothing? Poet is confounded'

parts.note: taken as written
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters of Poet are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poet, baffled, wonders if a basic form is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is confounded' rearranges POET into TOPE. 'Elementary' means of a chemical element, not simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant of a chemical element with a different number of neutrons.

clue.text: He wrote poems to the old army girls

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the women's branch of the British Army

explanation.surface: A poet dedicating verse to the women of the old army.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS was the women's branch of the British Army in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Snug part, sounds exquisite for Flora

indicators.note: sounds says the word for exquisite is taken as it is spoken, then written to fit the flower's spelling

parts.note: an exquisite is an old word for a dandy, an over-dressed man
Snug the joiner plays the Lion in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A cosy corner sounding elegant, for a woman named Flora.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, Snug plays the Lion; 'exquisite' as a noun is a fop. Said together these sound like the yellow flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora means plant life, and this yellow weed is one example.
